newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks soar by lunch on IMF hopes.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks soar by lunch on IMF hopes.

text.p: Thai stocks rose 4.67 percent by lunch on Wedenesday as hopes continued to grow that the IMF would be invited to assist Thai authorities in dealing with the country's economic problems, analysts and brokers said.
The SET index rose 29.22 points to 654.88. The SET 50 gained 2.82 points, or 6.02 percent, to 49.63. Turnover was active at 4.1 billion baht.

Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya's departure to Tokyo tonight to talk with his Japanese counterpart Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was raising investor hopes that an IMF package backed by Japanese money was in the offing, analysts said.

"It is thought unlikely that Thanong will come back empty-handed. An IMF package would go down pretty well with the market and it's given sentiment a bit of a lift," said Barry Yates, head of regional research at Seamico Securities.
A lack of sound economic management following the baht's flotation had reduced confidence and investors believed the IMF's involvement would help restore credibility, brokers said.
Most blue chips posted strong gains in response as investors gambled on the outcome of the meeting, traders said.
Buying was foreign led and premiums on the foreign board were also up, traders said.
On the main board Bangkok Bank Plc gained 15 baht to 180, Thai Farmers Bank Plc added eight to 114, finance and securities firm Phatra Thanakit Plc rose 4.50 to 49.75.
